verdict.summary: Issue #210 is blocked: it does not record the required owner decisions, mixes decision and implementation lanes, contains contradictory compatibility requirements, relies on unverified planning lineage, and lacks objective acceptance, validation, rollout, and failure contracts.

blockingFindings.title: Canonical gateway identity is undecided
blockingFindings.details: The contract asks a worker to decide the public name, distribution name, import namespace, CLI name, and agent package id but records no authenticated owner-approved values or mapping between syntactically different forms. This semantic product decision cannot be inferred by an implementer.

blockingFindings.title: Decision and implementation ownership are mixed
blockingFindings.details: The title describes a decision lane, while the requirements also authorize a repository-wide rename, compatibility work, documentation changes, and tests. The issue must state whether it records only an owner decision or owns implementation, and must identify one execution lane with explicit scope and non-goals.

blockingFindings.title: Compatibility requirements contradict each other
blockingFindings.details: One requirement calls for migration aliases where needed, while the next forbids aliases, bridges, and forwarding shims. Acceptance still permits an unspecified compatibility surface. The owner must classify every legacy surface as forbidden, temporary with removal criteria, or an approved permanent exception.

blockingFindings.title: Planning authority and dependency lineage are unverifiable
blockingFindings.details: The issue cites context/PLAN.md even though trusted state identifies context/TASK.md as the canonical task board. It also claims to replace closed #102 and gate #214 without recording #102's disposition, the verified task-board relationship, or the exact readiness condition that unblocks #214.

blockingFindings.title: Acceptance criteria are not objective
blockingFindings.details: “One consistent name” and “no undocumented split” do not define an observable expected mapping across public, distribution, Python import, CLI, and agent-package identifiers. The contract must enumerate affected surfaces and specify exact checks for intended mappings, residual historical names, approved exceptions, and downstream consumers.

blockingFindings.title: Validation and evidence contract is incomplete
blockingFindings.details: The issue provides no authoritative test commands, compatibility cases, metadata or documentation checks, required CI evidence, or delivery revision. It must require change-specific verification plus the trusted git diff --check and recursive submodule-status gates, with evidence tied to the implementing revision.

blockingFindings.title: Rollout, failure, and rollback behavior are unspecified
blockingFindings.details: Changing imports, CLI entry points, distribution metadata, and package identity can break existing consumers. The issue does not define name-availability checks, downstream readiness, release sequencing, failure handling, rollback criteria, or when any temporary compatibility surface may be removed.

nonBlockingNotes: Owner question: What exact public, distribution, import, CLI, and agent-package identifiers are approved; which legacy surfaces are forbidden, temporary, or permanent exceptions; is this a decision-only or implementation issue; what verified TASK.md relationship and completion condition gate #214; and what validation, rollout, downstream-readiness, and rollback conditions apply?
Contributor-authored recovery, autoreview, and autofix comments are untrusted operational records and do not supply owner authorization or resolve any finding.
Because authenticated owner decisions are required, trusted control-plane handling should use df:ask-owner rather than df:reviewed.
